original_question: Let f : X -> P^N be the blow-up of distinct points p_1, ..., p_r with exceptional divisors E_1, ..., E_r, and let D = dH - m_1 E_1 - ... - m_r E_r where H is the pullback of a hyperplane. Is there a general way to determine whether the divisor D is semi-effective, meaning that h^0(X, nD) > 0 for some integer n > 0?
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s target very closely: it uses the same blow-up setup X -> P^N at distinct points p_1, ..., p_r, the same divisor class D = dH - m_1E_1 - ... - m_rE_r, and the same notion of semi-effectivity via the existence of some n > 0 with h^0(X, nD) > 0. It also asks essentially the same decision problem as the paper’s official formulation.
missing_details: The paper assumes an algebraically closed ground field k of arbitrary characteristic.
Strictly speaking, semi-effectivity is defined in Definition 2.2.1 for a line bundle L on X; in this divisor notation one means the line bundle O_X(D).
The hyperplane class is written as H = f^*(O_{P^N}(1)), i.e. the pullback of the hyperplane class from P^N.
The coefficients d, m_1, ..., m_r are implicit integers, since D is an integral divisor class on the blow-up.
The paper poses the problem for arbitrary distinct points p_i in P^N; genericity is introduced only in the subsequent examples, not in the formal problem statement.

The nearby context adds a weighted Waldschmidt-type asymptotic criterion that gives sufficient conditions for semi-effectivity or non-semi-effectivity away from the boundary case e(sum m_i p_i)/r = d/(sum m_i); your draft does not mention this contextual sharpening.
refined_question: Over an algebraically closed field k of arbitrary characteristic, let f: X -> P^N be the blow-up of distinct points p_1, ..., p_r with exceptional divisors E_1, ..., E_r, and let H = f^*(O_{P^N}(1)). For the integral divisor D = dH - sum_{i=1}^r m_i E_i on X, is there a way to determine whether O_X(D) is semi-effective; that is, whether there exists an integer n > 0 such that h^0(X, O_X(nD)) > 0?
justification: The draft is essentially a paraphrase of the paper’s exact open problem in Section 2.2. Definition 2.2.1 supplies the paper’s meaning of “semi-effective,” and Problem 2.2.2 asks exactly whether one can determine semi-effectivity for divisors of the form dH - sum m_iE_i on the blow-up of distinct points of P^N. The paragraph immediately following the problem is the key nearby context: it explains that weighted Waldschmidt-type limits are relevant, gives one-sided criteria for semi-effectivity versus non-semi-effectivity, and isolates the unresolved boundary case. Section 3.10 then provides the worked example showing that 13H - 5E_1 - 4E_2 - ... - 4E_10 is not semi-effective.
